scenes.heading: Tracking, Analytics, and Optimizing Your Affiliate Income

sents.d: Tracking, Analytics, and Optimizing Your Affiliate Income
How to measure what's working, what's not, and where to focus your energy for maximum earnings.
EPC (Earnings Per Click): Your total commissions divided by total clicks.
This is the single most important metric — it tells you how much each click is worth.
Conversion Rate: The percentage of clicks that become sales.
Click-Through Rate: The percentage of your audience that actually clicks your links.
Revenue per piece of content: Which posts/videos earn the most?
Focus there.
Most affiliate dashboards show clicks and conversions, but you need to track WHERE the clicks come from.
Use SubIDs (most programs support them) to tag which page, video, or platform drove each click.
Example: your Amazon link for a product on your blog gets SubID "blog-review-jan" while the same product on TikTok gets "tiktok-review-jan." Now you know exactly which content performs.
Create a simple spreadsheet: Content Title | Platform | Date Published | Program | Clicks (30 days) | Sales | Commission | EPC.
Update it monthly.
After 3 months you'll see patterns: which platforms convert best, which products sell, and which content types drive the most revenue.
This data is more valuable than any course.
A/B test link placements in your content (beginning vs. middle vs. end).
Try different CTAs (calls to action).
Update old content with better-converting products.
Double down on your top 3 performing pieces — make more content like them.
Kill or update content that gets clicks but no conversions (wrong audience or wrong product).
Swap low-EPC programs for higher-paying alternatives.
Month 1-3: Learning, experimenting, probably earning $0-50.
Month 3-6: Finding what works, earning $50-500 if you're consistent.
Month 6-12: Optimizing winners, scaling content, $500-2000+.
Year 2+: Evergreen content compounds, recurring commissions stack, $2000-10,000+/month is realistic for serious creators.
Affiliate marketing is a slow build — the people who quit at month 2 miss the payoff at month 8.

take: Track clicks, conversions and earnings, then double down on what works.
